unit: Approval Gate checks 7b and 7b-2 (fail-closed send blocking)
description: No Communications row is left indefinitely in OUTBOUND_PENDING or OUTBOUND_UNCERTAIN, because each one permanently blocks any further send on that delivery key.
why_it_exists: OUTBOUND_PENDING means a run reached the send step and nothing confirmed the outcome. OUTBOUND_UNCERTAIN was added by F-04, after it was found that Mark Send Failed stamped every send-path error as OUTBOUND_FAILED - including a network timeout that may have occurred AFTER Gmail accepted the message. Because check 7c deliberately ignores OUTBOUND_FAILED so a known failure does not block a retry, an uncertain outcome was being converted into permission to send the same legal communication twice. Both states now block exactly like a duplicate, so each one is a live, human-owned obstruction that has to be counted and cleared.

blocking_semantics.OUTBOUND: blocks any further send on that action outright (check 7a)
blocking_semantics.OUTBOUND_PENDING: blocks when its idempotency_key equals the current send_key (check 7b)
blocking_semantics.OUTBOUND_UNCERTAIN: blocks when its idempotency_key equals the current send_key (check 7b-2)
blocking_semantics.OUTBOUND_FAILED: deliberately does NOT block - only for outcomes proven never to have reached Gmail (check 7c)
blocking_semantics.OUTBOUND_DRY_RUN: never blocks a later real send

assertions: Zero Communications rows have direction OUTBOUND_PENDING.
Zero Communications rows have direction OUTBOUND_UNCERTAIN.

Any such row that does exist must be reported with its communication_id, idempotency_key, approval_id, draft_id, action_id and recipient, because clearing it is a human decision (check the sent mail) and not an automatable one.
OUTBOUND_FAILED must never be used for an outcome that cannot be proven never to have reached Gmail - that is what OUTBOUND_UNCERTAIN is for.
target_unresolved_reason: kind is "invariant": not executed by harness/run.js.
